AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Wild Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Wild Animals.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Wild Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Wild Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Wild Animals.

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation.

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

5. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

7. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Food Nutrients.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Nutrients.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Nutrients.

11. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

13. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food Frying Frying? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food Frying Frying.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Repairing Garments 11 4.2 Constructing Innovative Gardens 14 Total Number of Les and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Repairing Garments and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Constructing Innovative Gardens gardens gardens and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Soil Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Wild Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
